- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction, especially in early forecast periods.
- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33), model underestimates; apply upward bias correction, particularly for the first 5–7 days of forecast horizon.
- Model often overshoots after sharp sentiment spikes (e.g., sentiment jumps to 1.00), leading to over-forecasted peaks; cap forecast peaks at 1.2x the prior 3-day average.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day forecasts: if forecast is >2.5x recent average, reduce by 20–40% unless sentiment supports sustained trend.
- Forecast horizon 1–7 days: model underperforms when sentiment is volatile; use 3-day moving average of history to anchor short-term forecasts.
- Forecast horizon 8–30 days: model tends to overreact to sentiment shifts; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 5-day exponential decay) to reduce noise in sentiment-driven spikes.
